author: Philly Leader
title: University of Pennsylvania's Kumari Lewis named new head coach for Alabama rowing
text:
Mike Mahoney Athletic Communications | Penn Athletics
Mike Mahoney Athletic Communications | Penn Athletics
Kumari Lewis, the associate head coach and recruiting coordinator for women's rowing at the University of Pennsylvania, has resigned to become the head coach for women's rowing at the University of Alabama. Lewis spent eight years with Penn's Quakers, beginning as an assistant coach before being promoted to associate head coach and recruiting coordinator ahead of the 2023-24 season.
"I could not be more grateful to the Penn community," said Lewis. "These last eight years at Penn have shaped who I am as a person and coach and it is certainly bittersweet to be leaving. I am grateful for all the doors my time at Penn has opened up, and I am excited for this next adventure in Tuscaloosa. That said, PWC will always hold a piece of my heart."
Penn's head coach Bill Manning praised Lewis' contributions: "What a great hire for Alabama," he stated. "Kumari has helped elevate Penn Women's Rowing to where we stand today: a consistent NCAA Championships competitor and highly ranked team. It's hard to overstate her contributions to the increased success the program has experienced these past five years."
Manning added that Alabama is gaining a head coach committed to her athletes' welfare and competitive success. He expressed confidence in her readiness for this new role.
During Lewis' tenure, Penn made significant achievements including their first four full-team appearances at the NCAA Championship from 2022-25. The Quakers improved their standings significantly during these years, reaching sixth place overall in 2023.
Additionally, under Lewis' guidance, Penn's teams won five medals at the Ivy League Championship across various categories.
Following the 2023 spring season, Lewis was part of a coaching staff named Collegiate Rowing Coaches Association (CRCA) Region I Staff of the Year alongside head coach Wesley Ng and assistant Helen Samaniego.
For updates on Penn women's rowing, follow @PennWomensRowing on Instagram or visit their website at PennAthletics.com.
